findings.title: Keyboard Tab order jumps backward across the screen in the expanded dialog
findings.claim: In the real-Chromium expanded dialog (what_if:true, plan-chart page), pressing Tab repeatedly from the dialog's start visits at least one pair of consecutive stops where the later stop sits above and not to the right of the earlier one, at every one of the three required viewports (375x812, 768x1024, 1280x800), so a sighted keyboard-only user's focus indicator jumps backward up the screen instead of following reading order.
findings.mechanism: The what-if panel's action row (`.wi-row.wi-actions`: apply/save/reset) and an earlier revert control (`.wi-revert`) sit inside `.whatif .wi-row { flex-wrap: wrap; ... }` rows; flex-wrap lets a later DOM child land visually above/left of an earlier one once the row wraps or the section above it reflows, but Tab order still follows DOM order, so the two orders diverge without the CSS engine or the card doing anything to keep them aligned.

findings.instrumented_symbol: custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/www/heatpump-optimizer-card.js:WhatIfPanel.html (the `.whatif .wi-row` / `.wi-actions` markup) driven through real `page.keyboard.press("Tab")` in Chromium

perturbation.change: One-line production CSS edit: `.whatif .wi-row { flex-wrap: wrap; ... }` -> `flex-wrap: nowrap;` (tools/audit/round8/D4/s1_tab_order.mjs reproduces the edit and restores the file in a finally-equivalent copy-back)

findings.metric_definition: inversions = # consecutive Tab stops where stop i+1's top is >0.6 row-heights above stop i's and not to its right (backward jump), via getBoundingClientRect().
findings.phenomenon_property: any focusable element inside a `flex-wrap: wrap` row group in the expanded dialog whose DOM position does not match its wrapped visual position on the current viewport
findings.seam_rule: grep -n "flex-wrap: wrap" custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/www/heatpump-optimizer-card.js (marks each CSS rule class whose rows can host a DOM/visual order mismatch; s1_tab_order.mjs's per-viewport Tab walk enumerates which rows actually invert)
reproduction_steps: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub with the 5 BLAS thread vars =1
HPO_PLANDATA=<path from tests/plan_view.py> HPO_VP_W=375 HPO_VP_H=812 node tools/audit/round8/D4/s1_tab_order.mjs
observe 'RESULT inversions=3 count' and the printed (from,to) pairs
findings.proposed_fix_scope: Reorder the `.wi-actions` / `.wi-row` markup (or the revert control's position) so DOM order matches the wrapped visual order at all three required viewports, or give the wrapping rows an explicit `order:` that tracks their visual position; re-run s1_tab_order.mjs at 375/768/1280 and require inversions=0 at each.
